reason: Both starters own elite recent form — Rodriguez at a 2.76 xERA over his last 3 and Lambert at 2.65 xERA over his last 3 — and each faces a punchless lineup: HOU is a 68 wRC+ vs RHP over its last 6 (75 over its last 12) and LAA a 94 wRC+ vs RHP over its last 6 (83 over its last 12). Both bullpens back it up, HOU at 3.06 xERA and LAA at 2.58 xERA over their last 12. Two elite arms against two poor offenses with quality relief behind them does not support a 8.5, and the market has this priced as an average run environment.

The line sits well below his recent output, and even a short leash does not threaten it given how many he misses per inning.

MIL makes plenty of contact at a 21.8 K% vs RHP over its last 6 with a 53.1 HH%, so there is no whiff spike coming. A line of 4.5 nearly doubles his recent per-start total, and getting plus money on the under is a clear mispricing.

Gasser has held up at home with a 3.55 ERA over his last 3 there and MIL has won its last 5 home starts behind him, while SEA's road bats managed just 3.0 runs per game over their last 5 SP starts. At home with that relief edge, MIL is worth more than this near-coinflip price.

STL brings the better lineup at 121 wRC+ vs RHP over its last 6 (105 over its last 12) against Singer's 4.81 xERA over his last 3. For a team holding both the pitching and hitting edge, -106 is well short of what this matchup deserves.

He works deep at 6.0 IP/gs over his last 3, so the innings are there. Priced at plus money, the market is leaning on his modest overall strikeout rate and ignoring how he has actually carved up this specific lineup.

His recent strikeout totals were built against high-whiff lineups (HOU 26%, NYY 30%), inflating his 19.7 K% over his last 3. Getting plus money on the under against a contact-heavy lineup he already fails to miss bats against is a clear overpay on the over.

CHW's offense is scorching at 137 wRC+ vs RHP over its last 6 and 123 over its last 12 against Holmes' 4.16 xERA over his last 3, while ATL is cold at 88 wRC+ vs LHP over its last 6. CHW also owns the far better relief corps at 3.33 xERA over its last 12 versus ATL's 4.21. For the home side holding the offensive and bullpen edges, an even-money price undervalues them.

Bradish is only average at 4.22 xERA over his last 3, but the market is pricing this half as if a normal offense is scoring; a lineup producing at that rate rarely reaches 3.5, and the plus price on the under is the mispricing.

Texas puts the ball in play, striking out just 19.8% vs LHP over its last 6, and Alvarez misses few bats himself at a 16.9% strikeout rate over his last 3 (5, 2, and 4 Ks). His recent strikeout totals were built against high-strikeout CIN (35%) and NYM (27%) lineups, so today's contact-heavy opponent should knock them down further, and the market hasn't fully faded the number.
